findings.message: The new smoke check can pass when a file is not actually served. `curl -sf` without `-w '%{http_code}'` only fails on 4xx/5xx, so a 3xx counts as success. That breaks AC-2, which says the job must fail on anything other than 200. The container is also started without DATABASE_URL, which leaves `guarded` null in apps/web/proxy.ts:11. So the check runs in guest-preview mode, where the signed-out gate never runs. The deployed image is gated, and that gate is exactly what a signed-out visitor goes through. The step therefore does not test what the marketing page's visitors get: a proxy matcher change that stops excluding one of these files would redirect it to /signin in production, and CI would stay green. Fix: assert the exact status code for each file (`test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' …)" = 200`). Also run the smoke container with a DATABASE_URL/auth config so the gate is live, for example a throwaway postgres service container. A unit test of the matcher against these five paths would also work.
findings.scenario: apps/web/proxy.ts matcher drops `vtt` from the marketing exclusion. In production (DATABASE_URL set), GET /marketing/amax-product.en.vtt gets a 307 to /signin and the captions never load. In CI the container has no DATABASE_URL, so the gate is off and the file returns 200; even with the gate on, `curl -sf` accepts the 307. The step passes either way.

findings.message: When the range request or the content-type check fails, the step exits with no message and no `docker logs amax`. The `/healthz` step above does print the logs. The two checks are also bare `test` and `grep -q` lines, so the log does not say which assertion failed or what status or header came back. Print the actual code and headers, and dump `docker logs amax` on failure, as the health step does.
findings.scenario: The image returns 200 instead of 206 for `Range: bytes=0-1023` → the job fails with exit 1 and no output naming the range check or the status it got.
